indexing: Life/examples step indexes are zero-based; outline numbered acts keep their written numbers, with frame act 0. fields names top-level JSON metadata.

rulings.defect: The ten GraphQL exemptions and one client-credentials exemption concern operations already served: query.issues, query.projects, query.viewer and oauthToken. Their reason is only that the twin has not implemented valid published fields or the supported grant. Linear’s own filtering/OAuth pages document them. Missing modeling is a twin defect; it is not evidence no World can replay them.
rulings.requiredChange: Remove all eleven current notReplayed entries. After step 33 add one replay for each recorded id, with the exact published request or response-bearing grant, replacing only documented placeholder ids by captures. Implement the needed documented fields/filters and enabled client-credentials app setting/team access before replay. Keep disabled-client-credentials example 33 as the documented disabled configuration, and create a separate enabled application via its settings door for the successful grant. Every replay must expect the published status, contain no undocumented GraphQL error in place of success, assert values its fixture decides, and carry only necessary vendor-API setup. Correct doc-examples client-credentials response output to retain all four published keys, including access_token and scope. Also vendor/replay the missing issueCreate example on the OAuth actor authorization page, whose createAsUser/displayIconUrl surface is already served. New example steps and their necessary setup may be appended at the named step 33; fields may change for notReplayed only.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects; https://linear.app/developers/filtering; https://linear.app/developers/oauth-2-0-authentication; https://linear.app/developers/oauth-actor-authorization

rulings.defect: The setup repeats the same consent/password problem as the life.
rulings.requiredChange: Authenticate at step 4 and capture an opaque browser session cookie; use that cookie and omit email/password at consent step 5. Necessary added sign-in/consent requests belong to these named steps.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Who is on a screen; https://linear.app/developers/oauth-2-0-authentication

rulings.defect: Project creation (10), another teams list (11) and project read (12) form their own create/discover/read verification chain. None makes a current replay’s precondition true or reads an example mutation’s effect; a team id is already captured by step 9.
rulings.requiredChange: Remove step 11. Remove steps 10 and 12, or repurpose them as genuinely necessary fixture setup for the newly required published project/issue filters: step 10 may create the project and documented lead/state relations needed by a published example; step 12 may supply only data actually needed by that fixture, not repeat a known project read just to verify setup. Any fixture relation must use the vendor’s API, and later example expectations must assert the decided relations.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects

rulings.defect: Step 13 pins Todo and Done and the presence of a seventh state even though no setup writes those names/counts and the schema only says teamCreate creates default states. Step 21 pins Todo by a literal again. Published examples prohibit asserting generated/default values as guessed fixture output.
rulings.requiredChange: In step 13 retain the state-discovery request needed by IssueUpdate, capture the chosen state id and its actual name from the response, and remove the literal default names and seven-state assertion. In step 20 assert the returned state name against that captured name alongside its captured id. In step 21 assert the already captured state id occurs; leave uncaptured server-default names undecided with the reason. Remove unused backlog/done captures unless a required published-example fixture needs them.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects; linear/spec/schema.graphql.gz: Mutation.teamCreate

rulings.defect: The personal viewer and team examples use substring expectations for setup-decided full names. They could accept a different full name despite exact values supplied at setup.
rulings.requiredChange: At 14 assert data.viewer.name equals Maya Chen. At 15 assert data.teams.nodes.0.name equals Booking App. Keep the captured id/email checks.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects

rulings.defect: The users example checks only whether some rendered node contains Jonah. Setup has decided three known users and their ids/names (Maya, Jonah and Fieldbook), so the other decided returned members are unverified.
rulings.requiredChange: Assert that the returned users include all three captured ids and their known names, using order-independent expectations, and close the result set at the three members the fixture creates. Do not invent the vendor’s ordering for equal timestamps.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects

rulings.defect: These published reads leave setup-decided values unchecked: team issues omit the supplied description; the paged issue omits its updated title and page completion after the single created issue; recently updated issues omit their supplied title and setup-caused creation/update times; high-priority reads omit their supplied title.
rulings.requiredChange: At 19 assert the issue description equals More detailed error report in markdown. At 22 assert the node title equals New Issue Title and hasNextPage is false because the fixture holds exactly one issue within first:10; leave opaque cursor values unpinned. At 24 assert the title and the World-clock creation/update instants caused by steps 17/20 (derive these from the actual journey clock rather than guessing a vendor default); mark the generated identifier undecided rather than pinning the numbering sequence. At 27 assert the supplied title. In any affected read, close the single-issue collection only because setup determines its membership, and do not assert generated cursors or ids by literal.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects

rulings.defect: priority equals 0 is a vendor-applied default, not a value set by the fixture. It is pinned as though supplied by setup.
rulings.requiredChange: Remove the numeric equality on data.issues.nodes.0.priority and name that path in undecided, explaining that no priority was supplied and Linear applies the documented no-priority default. Keep the captured issue id and decided title checks; the subsequent exclusion example may assert its empty result as the documented predicate’s effect on this fixture.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects; https://linear.app/developers/filtering

rulings.defect: The step is named a dropped response, but step 31 receives and captures both new tokens and there is no fault/dropped-response action. The sent request demonstrates grace-period replay, not an observed lost response.
rulings.requiredChange: Rename step 32 to state that replaying the prior refresh request within the documented grace period returns the same token pair. Keep its request and comparison to captured newAccess/newRefresh; do not claim the harness simulated a dropped response.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects; https://linear.app/developers/oauth-2-0-authentication

doubts.doubt: The disabled-client-credentials body is a faithful vendor refusal, but its page does not explicitly state the HTTP status. The locally authored OAuth spec chooses 400, which is plausible; no contradictory published status was found.

notes: Read the complete outline, all 44 customer-life steps, all 34 examples steps, all 33 vendored documentation example entries, and every one of 11 notReplayed reasons. Reviewed the SDL fields/inputs and vendor pages for GraphQL, pagination, filtering, OAuth, OAuth actor authorization, and deprecations. No suite reruns and no pack implementation/story edits.

Every bar item was applied: refusal causes; repeats and sitting boundaries; state toggles; kept promises; feature-tour padding; read need; actors and learned identifiers; era; vendor contradictions; payload/name fidelity; and documented doors.

The reported green checks were treated as orientation only, not proof of plausibility. No second judging is requested: the author must apply this complete ruling set once and carry the verdict mechanically.
